wu: Flashcard Speed Review: Hold up clothing flashcards (jeans, t-shirt, dress, jacket, sneakers, scarf); students shout the English word and a price in Moroccan Dirhams. Teacher asks 'How much is/are...?' to prompt full sentences.
wuAlt: Price Guessing Game: Teacher mimes putting on an item; students guess 'Is it 100 DH?' until correct.
Clothes Charades: Students act out wearing an item; others guess 'Are you wearing a hat?'
pres: Show a too-small t-shirt and too-big jeans; ask 'Why can't I wear this?' Elicit 'It's too small/big.' Drill model sentences: 'This shirt is too small for me.' 'These jeans aren't big enough.' Check with thumbs-up/down: 'Is this jacket too warm?'
presAlt: Realia Display: Bring in actual clothes; students compare sizes with 'too/ enough'.
Storytime: Show a comic strip of a shopping fail; students identify problems with 'too/ enough'.
prac: Worksheet Gap-Fill: Complete sentences like 'This dress is _____ expensive.' with 'too' or 'enough'. Pair Drill: Student A describes an item ('This coat is not warm enough.'); Student B responds with a solution ('Try this one.')
pracAlt: Board Race: Two teams race to write 'too/ enough' sentences about clothing items.
Chain Drill: Students take turns adding to a story: 'I bought a shirt, but it was too small...'.
ls: Listen to a dialogue at a clothing store where a customer exchanges items; students tick problems (size/ color/ price) on a worksheet. Play twice: first for gist, second for details.
re: Simon Says with 'too/ enough': 'Simon says touch something too expensive!' Students mime touching an item and saying 'This is too expensive!'
prod: Roleplay Shop Exchange: In pairs, one is a customer returning a shirt (too small), one is a shop assistant. Use target language: 'This shirt is too small.' 'Do you have a bigger size?' 'These are not long enough.' Swap roles.
rw: Read a short product review about sneakers; underline all sentences with 'too/ enough'. Then write 2-3 sentences reviewing a Moroccan market item using the same structure.
st: Read a short story about a teen's shopping trip in Oujda; discuss with partners: 'What was too expensive?' End with 'Today we learned to negotiate with too/ enough. Thank you, class!'
g: Students bargain with fake Dirhams: '50 DH!' 'Too cheap! 100 DH!'
Call out 'too big/small'; students cross off matching clothing items.
Students walk and describe outfits: 'This hat is too colorful!'
Students remember prices of items and say 'The jeans are too expensive!'
Students swap items and explain why they can't use them.
diff: Fast finishers: Design a poster for a 'too/ enough' sale with slogans like 'Jeans too cheap? No! Enough cheap!'
Support: Use sentence starters: 'This is too _____.' 'These are not _____ enough.'
hw: Write a 25+ word email to a friend about shopping in Oujda; use 'too/ enough'.
Record a 1-minute video review of a local clothing store; mention prices and sizes.
Draw 3 clothing items and write sentences: 'This scarf is too warm.' 'These shoes are not comfortable enough.'
tip: Use local currency (DH) and Moroccan shopping contexts (souks, bargaining culture) to make the language relevant and boost engagement.
